newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end down on LME losses.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end down on LME losses.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended down slightly on Thursday following overnight losses on the London Metal Exchange (LME), trader said.
The most active June 1997 contract ended at 23,590 yuan ($2,843) per tonne, losing 10 yuan. It opened at 23,420 yuan, hitting an intraday low of 23,400 and a high of 23,620.
March fell 80 to 23,070, April 70 to 23,320, May 50 to 23,500, July 20 to 23,560 and August 140 to 23,450.
Combined volume fell to 42,200 tonnes from 56,040.
Copper opened lower and most contracts moved in a narrow range at low levels for most of the session.
Traders said overnight LME losses discouraged some long position holders but most investors ignored the London falls and remained on the sidelines.
"LME losses triggered some profit-taking by retail investors who dominated the day's trading," one trader said. "But most investors were staying on the sidelines with market direction unclear."
Traders said copper was unlikely to move out of a narrow range of consolidation in the short term due to a lack of market-moving news.
"Copper was digesting heavy gains gathered since the Chinese lunar new year holiday last month, waiting for fresh market-moving news," a second trader said.
Aluminium ended down on a correction after gains on Wednesday. March fell 80 yuan to 15,900 yuan ($1,916) per tonne, April 70 to 16,300, May 100 to 16,600 and June 100 to 16,850.
Combined volume fell to 4,120 tonnes from 6,280.
